response: Yes, end-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO2) measurement has been found to correlate with arterial carbon dioxide (PaCO2) in extremely low birth weight infants in the first week of life. However, the correlation may not always be precise, and factors such as respiratory support, lung disease, and hemodynamic instability can affect the accuracy of the correlation. Nonetheless, ETCO2 can be a useful non-invasive tool for monitoring and trending carbon dioxide levels in these vulnerable patients.
